recipes.name: Baked Brunch Omelet
ingredients_raw: 0.5 (1 pound) loaf white bread, cut into cubes
1 dash hot pepper sauce, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13 inch baking pan.
Place half of the bread cubes on bottom of baking pan. Sprinkle with half of the ham and then half of the cheese; repeat.
In a large bowl, beat together eggs, milk, salt, hot sauce and green onions. Pour egg mixture into pan.
Place pan on top of a baking sheet with a rim and place in oven. Pour water into baking sheet and bake for 60 minutes, or until eggs have set.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is actually a very good breakfast casserole, but there are some key details missing. First you must use french bread in this recipe. You need all the crust to soak up the eggs and milk. I simply rip the loaf into bite size pieces with my hands, much easier than cubing it. Secondly, toss the bread, 1.5 cups ham cubes and 2-3 cups shredded cheese with 2-3 Tablespoons of flour before putting it all in the baking dish, it keeps the egg bake from being soggy. Then, blend the eggs/milk in the blender with the other ingredients (I add 3 Tablespoons margerine and 1 tsp. dry mustard) and pour over the bread mixture. Cover and let it sit overnight in the fridge allowing the bread time to absorb the liquid. It will look almost too dry the next morning, but it's supposed to. I bake it at 350 for about an hour, uncovering it at about forty minutes. I do not put it in a water bath. Enjoy!

I always shake my head when someone rates something 5 stars and then makes over the whole recipe! I make something very similar to this and it is my family's FAVORITE. I use regular bread and I do layer it - both "details" that I would leave the same as the recipe. Sometimes we substitute crispy bacon for ham. Oh - and we leave the bread in whole slices (minus the crust) and butter it. I suppose that is why we don't have to use the water pan. Another thing we add is some crushed Special K or corn flakes to the top just before baking with some melted butter sprinkled on top to prevent them from drying out. Adds some crisp. BUT...this omelet is GREAT just as it is written. We call ours the Christmas Morning Lifesaver! Great for company and if we need two, we do one ham and one bacon.

We had breakfast for dinner last night using this recipe, along with crispy bacon and a toasted English muffin. I made half of this recipe in an 8x8” square pan, which produced an omelet a little flatter than I would have liked, but that’s an easy fix for the next time. I cut way back on the amount of cheese, using a handful per layer, about one cup total. I used hamburger buns for the bread and I added some sautéed green and red bell peppers. Rather than putting the green onions in with the egg mixture, I just sprinkled them over each layer. My half recipe took 40 minutes to bake. Very good! I wouldn’t hesitate to make this again!

I've been making this same recipe (almost) for >35 years. My family loves it for Christmas breakfast! A couple of differences in mine: (13"x9" dish) I take off the crusts and just use the bread squares (wheat is great!); 2 cups of ham 2 cups of grated cheese over the bread and another layer of breakd. THEN 6 beaten eggs with 3 cups milk, 1/2 tsp salt and 1 tsp. dry mustard. Pour over the layers. The milk will absorb! Refrigerate over night (it works as well to bake immediately, though.) Before baking, add 2 cups crushed corn flakes, crackers or bread crumbs, then pour over 1/2 cup melted margarine. DO use a cookie sheet under the baking dish though, it may boil over in your oven. This recipe halves perfectly to fit in a 9" square baking dish for a smaller size. AND it is great for dinner with biscuits, applesauce or fruit! We call it "Christmas Brunch Souffle"!!

I substituted ingredients based on what I had on hand. I used an olive loaf cut into cubes, brushed the pieces with olive oil and broiled them until toasted on both sides. I substituted italian spicy sausage for the ham the first time I made it. Everybody loved it. The second time I used chorizo sausage, used only 16 oz of cheese, added 1 cup green onions and 1 cup of red peppers. That was awesome! Our guests couldn't stop eating. Great recipe Aetibesar ! Thanks for sharing :)

This is pretty good, I added a can or ortega chilies and some chopped red bell pepper. I suggest that you slightly beat your eggs before you add the milk. That way it is easier to mix and you know that all the yokes are cracked. It is really impossible to scoop out an egg after you pour it over the bread mixture, if you find it wasn't beaten enough. If using sourdough bread, let it sit for 30 minutes before baking

So easy and great to throw together in the evening and pop in the oven the next morning. I was reading the reviews about the texture and decided to cube the entire loaf of bread, instead of the 1/2 the recipe calls for. That worked perfectly with the amount of cheese it requires, but you may want to add a little extra ham. Will definitely do again and think about adding a little Dijon or green onion for some extra zing!

Delicious! Baked up tall and looked beautiful. Based on other contributors’ input, I used French bread, 2 types of cheese when layering, 1 t. dry mustard and 1 T. Worcestershire sauce. I did not put in water bath.

Will definitely make this again. So easy. Cut off crusts because I didn't have a lot of time to soak the bread. Did not use water bath. Done in 50 minutes. Looked and tasted great. For health reasons only used about a cup and a half of cheese.that was plenty. Also added a chopped tomato. Probably wouldn't add salt next time as ham was pretty salty. Contrary to another reviewer, I loved the leftovers.

I use a loaf of crusty French bread and add thinly sliced mushrooms and a cup of cooked, squeeze-dried spinach in the layers. I used 1 1/2 cups of liquid coffee mate, saves lots of calories, which I make up for by adding a couple of tbls melted butter and several scrapes of fresh nutmeg.

Outstanding!

I can't believe there's only one rating for this recipe! I absolutely love it! We have had this for several occasions and have created many variations. I've been asked for the recipe several times! Here are some ideas - red peppers are great in it. Meat lovers - with sausage, ham and bacon. We almost always put sweet onions in it no matter what combination we make. Adobo is the perfect spice option. Franks hot sauce is great in it. Even stale bread can be used and one time we made it in a cast iron skillet on the stove top - it was wonderful, just be sure to heat evenly, medium to low heat with a tight lid, but towards the end of cooking, prop the lid to let air in.
Simple recipe to prepare and it tastes amazing!
We make this every Christmas!
I’ve made this many times and it’s always a hit with family and friends. It’s easy to put together and can tolerate additions and deletions depending on what you have in your pantry.

Made this for mothers day brunch and it was amazing!!
I made it the night before. Reduced the amount of cheese.
Baked it without a water bathing it came out perfectly.
it was awesome!

Definately turned out much better than I expected. Minus the onions and pepper sauce (nobody in the house can tolerate them), it has the fewest ingredients of anything I've made yet. I will absolutely be shaking things up with other ingredients next time I make it (perhaps sausage and mushrooms in place of the ham).
One of my all-time favorites! I like to add lots of veggies.

This is a great basic egg bake recipe. Enjoy it as written, or substitute whatever meats/veggies/cheese you have on hand & proceed with putting it in the fridge overnight, then baking in the morning. I like adding garlic & onion powder & 1/2 tsp of. dry mustard or a couple of squirts of dijion mustard sometimes, too. Awesome for up at the lake when there's guests to feed & makes my morning less hectic.....just serve with some fruit and perhaps coffee cake or muffins and everyone's happy. I make a simple bacon & cheese only one, as well....to please the picky eaters in the crowd!

I used a bag of hash browns instead of the patties. It was tasty and turned out well. The only reasonl it didn't get 5 stars was that it wasn't very eggy although that may have been the difference in the kind of potatoes that I used. I will make it again and increase the eggs in it.
